entities.name: George Mouzalon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
George Mouzalon (died 1258) was a prominent Byzantine statesman and military commander who rose to become the *megas domestikos* (commander-in-chief) and chief minister under Emperor Theodore II Laskaris of the Empire of Nicaea. His career, spanning the mid-13th century, is emblematic of the internal power struggles and dynastic rivalries that characterized the Nicaean Empire's efforts to reclaim Constantinople and restore the Byzantine Empire after the Fourth Crusade. Mouzalon's meteoric ascent from humble origins to unprecedented influence at the imperial court profoundly challenged the established aristocracy, ultimately leading to his violent downfall.

Born into a modest family, George Mouzalon was a childhood companion and close confidant of Theodore II, who, upon his accession in 1254, elevated Mouzalon to positions of immense power, sidelining traditional noble families like the Philes and the Bourtzes. He was appointed *protosebastos* and *protovestiarios*, and later *megas domestikos*, effectively governing the empire alongside Theodore II. Mouzalon played a crucial role in the emperor's administrative reforms and military campaigns, including the successful defense against the Second Bulgarian Empire's incursions in 1255-1256 and diplomatic initiatives with the Despotate of Epirus. His influence extended to all facets of imperial policy, often at the expense of the entrenched aristocracy and the Orthodox Church hierarchy.
